correctness.rationale: For diagonal matching-field vertices, row \(i\) can use only columns \(i,\ldots,i+n-k\) and has row sum one. The resulting active-band row-sum affine space has dimension \(k(n-k)\), equal to the source dimension from Theorem 2.15, so it is the exact affine hull. Its orthogonal projection of the origin is uniform on each active row, with squared norm \(k/(n-k+1)\). Every vertex has squared norm \(k\) and scalar product \(k/(n-k+1)\) with the center, giving the displayed radius. The \(n-k+1\) consecutive-block vertices cover each active coordinate exactly once, so their average is the center; the parallel-axis identity then proves global minimum-enclosing optimality and uniqueness.

value.rationale: The diagonal matching-field polytope is the native exponent-vector realization of the Grassmannian Gelfand--Tsetlin polytope and the base object for mutation families of Newton--Okounkov bodies and toric degenerations. Its Euclidean metric is not preserved by the unimodular equivalence to the familiar order-polytope model, so an exact minimum enclosing sphere in these coordinates is genuinely realization-specific information. The theorem gives a closed all-\(k,n\) formula, shows every Pluecker-indexed vertex is a contact point, and supplies a sparse explicit positive certificate using only \(n-k+1\) consecutive minors.
